items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I hired Eddie Conlon, Mezzrow, Cliff Jackson, Frankie Newton and Davy Tough at seven dollars apiece, a college date, and I got ten for being leader and getting them together.

ctx.x: This was in New York between the years of 1938 and about '40. And we did work. We took jobs in Passaic, New Jersey, and we took a five dollar apiece job to sing for one night or something. We did anything to work. And we did find some work, because Frankie was the kind of guy that would charm the office girl. And he'd say to me, don't you go up there, let me go up there, I'll charm her. And he'd get to see the manager or the booking office man. And so that's what he would do and turn around, and -- but he was…

he sang. I wasn't ecstatic about it but I liked the way he sang, because he swung. He could swing. And at that time, it's not the Frankie Laine you hear now, he didn't have the same thing. Everything was off the cuff. Sing two choruses and the piano would take one, and sing another one.
